problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=3x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=3y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the decoupled system above?
worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]x(t)
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=3$ with the corresponding eigenvectors $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ and $[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

The general solution of the system is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]={e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Notice that for each vector $[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ we get the straight-line solutions of the form
${e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}]$
that represent the line passing through the origin and parallel to the vector $[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}].$

Since ${e}^{3t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions move away from the origin as $t\to \infty .$ 

Among the given options, the only phase portrait satisfying these conditions is the following:
